# Claw Code

English · 中文

start with the real crab-powered harnesses

github.com/code-yeongyu/lazycodex
github.com/Yeachan-Heo/gajae-code

Join the Discords: ultraworkers discord · gajae-code discord

> [!IMPORTANT] > **Claw Code is not the serious production project here.** > This repository is closer to a museum exhibit than a product pitch, a crustacean-run artifact kept alive by clawed gajaes, swept and labeled by agents, and automatically maintained according to the harnesses above. > > As already described in the project philosophy, this is not meant to be hand-operated like a normal product repo. It is an **agent-managed exhibit**: the harnesses plan, execute, verify, label, and preserve the artifact while the crabs keep the tank running. > > If you want to actually run work, start with **[LazyCodex](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/lazycodex)** or **[Gajae-Code](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/gajae-code)**. If you want to inspect the strange little fossil of the Claw Code moment, continue below. > > For the longer public explanation behind this philosophy, see [here](https://x.com/realsigridjin/status/2039472968624185713).

ultraworkers/claw-code · Usage · Rust workspace · Parity · Roadmap · Contributing · Security · UltraWorkers Discord

Claw Code is the public Rust implementation of the `claw` CLI agent harness. The canonical implementation lives in [`rust/`](./rust), and the current source of truth for this repository is **ultraworkers/claw-code**. > [!IMPORTANT] > Start with [`USAGE.md`](./USAGE.md) for build, auth, CLI, session, and parity-harness workflows. For file submission/navigation questions, see [Navigation and file context](./docs/navigation-file-context.md). For local OpenAI-compatible models and offline skill installs, see [Local OpenAI-compatible providers and skills setup](./docs/local-openai-compatible-providers.md). Windows users can jump to the PowerShell-first [Windows install and release quickstart](./docs/windows-install-release.md). Make `claw doctor` your first health check after building, use [`rust/README.md`](./rust/README.md) for crate-level details, read [`PARITY.md`](./PARITY.md) for the current Rust-port checkpoint, and see [`docs/container.md`](./docs/container.md) for the container-first workflow. > > **ACP / Zed status:** `claw-code` does not ship an ACP/Zed daemon or JSON-RPC entrypoint yet. Run `claw acp` (or `claw --acp`) for the current status instead of guessing from source layout; `claw acp serve` is currently a discoverability alias only, returns status with exit code 0, and real ACP support remains tracked separately in `ROADMAP.md`. For the public JSON contract, see [`docs/g011-acp-json-rpc-status-contract.md`](./docs/g011-acp-json-rpc-status-contract.md). ## Current repository shape - **`rust/`** — canonical Rust workspace and the `claw` CLI binary - **`USAGE.md`** — task-oriented usage guide for the current product surface - **`PARITY.md`** — Rust-port parity status and migration notes - **`ROADMAP.md`** — active roadmap and cleanup backlog - **`PHILOSOPHY.md`** — project intent and system-design framing - **`src/` + `tests/`** — companion Python/reference workspace and audit helpers; not the primary runtime surface ## Quick start > [!NOTE] > [!WARNING] > **`cargo install claw-code` installs the wrong thing.** The `claw-code` crate on crates.io is a deprecated stub that places `claw-code-deprecated.exe` — not `claw`. Running it only prints `"claw-code has been renamed to agent-code"`. **Do not use `cargo install claw-code`.** Either build from source (this repo) or install the upstream binary: > ```bash > cargo install agent-code # upstream binary — installs 'agent.exe' (Windows) / 'agent' (Unix), NOT 'agent-code' > ``` > This repo (`ultraworkers/claw-code`) is **build-from-source only** — follow the steps below. ```bash # 1. Clone and build git clone https://github.com/ultraworkers/claw-code cd claw-code/rust cargo build --workspace # 2. Set your API key (Anthropic API key — not a Claude subscription) export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..." # 3. Verify everything is wired correctly ./target/debug/claw doctor # 4. Run a prompt ./target/debug/claw prompt "say hello" # 5. Start an interactive session ./target/debug/claw ``` > [!NOTE] > **Windows (PowerShell):** the binary is `claw.exe`, not `claw`. Use `.\target\debug\claw.exe` or run `cargo run -- prompt "say hello"` to skip the path lookup. ### Windows setup **PowerShell is a supported Windows path.** Use whichever shell works for you. The common onboarding issues on Windows are: 1. **Install Rust first** — download from and run the installer. Close and reopen your terminal when it finishes. 2. **Verify Rust is on PATH:** ```powershell cargo --version ``` If this fails, reopen your terminal or run the PATH setup from the Rust installer output, then retry. 3. **Clone and build** (works in PowerShell, Git Bash, or WSL): ```powershell git clone https://github.com/ultraworkers/claw-code cd claw-code/rust cargo build --workspace ``` 4. **Run** (PowerShell — note `.exe` and backslash): ```powershell $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "sk-ant-..." .\target\debug\claw.exe prompt "say hello" ``` For release ZIPs, PATH setup, provider switching, and notification smoke checks, see [`docs/windows-install-release.md`](./docs/windows-install-release.md). **Git Bash / WSL** are optional alternatives, not requirements. If you prefer bash-style paths (`/c/Users/you/...` instead of `C:\Users\you\...`), Git Bash (ships with Git for Windows) works well. In Git Bash, the `MINGW64` prompt is expected and normal — not a broken install. ## Post-build: locate the binary and verify After running `cargo build --workspace`, the `claw` binary is built but **not** automatically installed to your system. Here's where to find it and how to verify the build succeeded. ### Binary location After `cargo build --workspace` in `claw-code/rust/`: **Debug build (default, faster compile):** - **macOS/Linux:** `rust/target/debug/claw` - **Windows:** `rust/target/debug/claw.exe` **Release build (optimized, slower compile):** - **macOS/Linux:** `rust/target/release/claw` - **Windows:** `rust/target/release/claw.exe` If you ran `cargo build` without `--release`, the binary is in the `debug/` folder. ### Verify the build succeeded Test the binary directly using its path: ```bash # macOS/Linux (debug build) ./rust/target/debug/claw --help ./rust/target/debug/claw doctor # Windows PowerShell (debug build) .\rust\target\debug\claw.exe --help .\rust\target\debug\claw.exe doctor ``` PowerShell smoke commands that do not require live credentials: ```powershell $env:CLAW_CONFIG_HOME = Join-Path $env:TEMP "claw config home" New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $env:CLAW_CONFIG_HOME | Out-Null Remove-Item Env:\ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, Env:\ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, Env:\OPENAI_API_KEY -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue .\rust\target\debug\claw.exe help .\rust\target\debug\claw.exe status .\rust\target\debug\claw.exe config env .\rust\target\debug\claw.exe doctor ``` If these commands succeed, the build is working. `claw doctor` is your first health check — it validates your API key, model access, and tool configuration. ### Optional: Add to PATH If you want to run `claw` from any directory without the full path, choose one of these approaches: **Option 1: Symlink (macOS/Linux)** ```bash ln -s $(pwd)/rust/target/debug/claw /usr/local/bin/claw ``` Then reload your shell and test: ```bash claw --help ``` **Option 2: Use `cargo install` (all platforms)** Build and install to Cargo's default location (`~/.cargo/bin/`, which is usually on PATH): ```bash # From the claw-code/rust/ directory cargo install --path . --force # Then from anywhere claw --help ``` **Option 3: Update shell profile (bash/zsh)** Add this line to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`: ```bash export PATH="$(pwd)/rust/target/debug:$PATH" ``` Reload your shell: ```bash source ~/.bashrc # or source ~/.zshrc claw --help ``` ### Troubleshooting - **"command not found: claw"** — The binary is in `rust/target/debug/claw`, but it's not on your PATH. Use the full path `./rust/target/debug/claw` or symlink/install as above. - **"permission denied"** — On macOS/Linux, you may need `chmod +x rust/target/debug/claw` if the executable bit isn't set (rare). - **Debug vs. release** — If the build is slow, you're in debug mode (default). Add `--release` to `cargo build` for faster runtime, but the build itself will take 5–10 minutes. > [!NOTE] > **Auth:** claw requires an **API key** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, etc.) — Claude subscription login is not a supported auth path. Run the workspace test suite after verifying the binary works: ```bash cd rust cargo test --workspace ``` ## Documentation map - [`USAGE.md`](./USAGE.md) — quick commands, auth, sessions, config, parity harness - [`docs/navigation-file-context.md`](./docs/navigation-file-context.md) — terminal navigation, scrollback, `@path` file context, attachments, and secret-safety guidance - [`docs/local-openai-compatible-providers.md`](./docs/local-openai-compatible-providers.md) — Ollama/llama.cpp/vLLM setup, Claw multi-provider positioning, and local skills install checks - [`docs/windows-install-release.md`](./docs/windows-install-release.md) — PowerShell-first install, release artifact, provider switching, and Windows/WSL notification smoke paths - [`rust/README.md`](./rust/README.md) — crate map, CLI surface, features, workspace layout - [`PARITY.md`](./PARITY.md) — parity status for the Rust port - [`rust/MOCK_PARITY_HARNESS.md`](./rust/MOCK_PARITY_HARNESS.md) — deterministic mock-service harness details - [`ROADMAP.md`](./ROADMAP.md) — active roadmap and open cleanup work - [`docs/g004-events-reports-contract.md`](./docs/g004-events-reports-contract.md) — Stream 2 lane event/report contract guidance for consumers - [`PHILOSOPHY.md`](./PHILOSOPHY.md) — why the project exists and how it is operated - [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md), [`SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md), [`SUPPORT.md`](./SUPPORT.md), and [`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) — contribution, vulnerability-reporting, support, and community policies - [`LICENSE`](./LICENSE) — MIT license for this repository ## Ecosystem Claw Code is built in the open alongside the broader UltraWorkers toolchain: - [clawhip](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/clawhip) - [oh-my-openagent](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent) - [oh-my-claudecode](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode) - [oh-my-codex](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex) - [gajae-code](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/gajae-code) - [UltraWorkers Discord](https://discord.gg/5TUQKqFWd) ## Ownership / affiliation disclaimer - This repository does **not** claim ownership of the original Claude Code source material. - This repository is **not affiliated with, endorsed by, or maintained by Anthropic**.

repos.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
repos.readme_excerpt:
# Superpowers

Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

## Table of Contents

- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Commercial Services](#commercial-services)
- [Getting Started](#installation)
  - [Claude Code](#claude-code)
  - [Antigravity](#antigravity)
  - [Codex App](#codex-app)
  - [Codex CLI](#codex-cli)
  - [Cursor](#cursor)
  - [Devin CLI](#devin-cli)
  - [Factory Droid](#factory-droid)
  - [Gemini CLI](#gemini-cli)
  - [GitHub Copilot CLI](#github-copilot-cli)
  - [Grok Build CLI](#grok-build-cli)
  - [Kimi Code](#kimi-code)
  - [OpenCode](#opencode)
  - [Pi](#pi)
  - [Qwen Code](#qwen-code)
  - [Hermes Agent](#hermes-agent)
  - [Muse](#muse)
- [The Basic Workflow](#the-basic-workflow)
- [When Something Goes Wrong](#when-something-goes-wrong)
- [Community](#community)
- [What's Inside](#whats-inside)
- [Philosophy](#philosophy)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [Updating](#updating)
- [License](#license)
- [Visual companion telemetry](#visual-companion-telemetry)

## How it works

It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. 

Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. 

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. 

Next up, once you say "go", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

## Commercial Services

If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com.

## Installation

Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

### Claude Code

Superpowers is available via the [official Claude plugin marketplace](https://claude.com/plugins/superpowers)

#### Official Marketplace

- Install the plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official
  ```

#### Superpowers Marketplace

The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
  ```

- Install the plugin from this marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
  ```

### Antigravity

Install Superpowers as a plugin from this repository:

```bash
agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
```

Antigravity lists each installed skill's description, and the description of
the `using-superpowers` skill prompts the model to load that skill at the start
of a conversation. Reinstall with the same command to update.

### Codex App

Superpowers is available via the [official Codex plugin marketplace](https://github.com/openai/plugins).

- In the Codex app, click on Plugins in the sidebar.
- You should see `Superpowers` in the Coding section.
- Click the `+` next to Superpowers and follow the prompts.

### Codex CLI

Superpowers is available via the [official Codex plugin marketplace](https://github.com/openai/plugins).

- Open the plugin search interface:

  ```bash
  /plugins
  ```

- Search for Superpowers:

  ```bash
  superpowers
  ```

- Select `Install Plugin`.

### Cursor

- In Cursor Agent chat, install from marketplace:

  ```text
  /add-plugin superpowers
  ```

- Or search for "superpowers" in the plugin marketplace.

### Devin CLI

- Install the plugin from this repository:

  ```bash
  devin plugins install obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update to the latest version with:

  ```bash
  devin plugins update superpowers
  ```

### Factory Droid

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Install the plugin:

  ```bash
  droid plugin install superpowers@superpowers
  ```

### Gemini CLI

- Install the extension:

  ```bash
  gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  gemini extensions update superpowers
  ```

### GitHub Copilot CLI

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
  ```

- Install the plugin:

  ```bash
  copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
  ```

### Grok Build CLI

Superpowers is available via the [official Grok plugin marketplace](https://github.com/xai-org/plugin-marketplace).

- Install the plugin from xAI's official marketplace:

  ```bash
  grok plugin install superpowers@xai-official --trust
  ```

- Or open the marketplace in the TUI, search for Superpowers, and install it:

  ```text
  /marketplace
  ```

### Kimi Code

Superpowers is available in Kimi Code's plugin marketplace.

- Open Kimi Code's plugin manager:

  ```text
  /plugins
  ```

- Go to `Marketplace` > `Superpowers` and install it.

- Or install directly from this repository:

  ```text
  /plugins install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Detailed docs: [docs/README.kimi.md](docs/README.kimi.md)

### OpenCode

OpenCode uses its own plugin install; install Superpowers separately even if you
already use it in another harness.

- Tell OpenCode:

  ```
  Fetch and follow instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obra/superpowers/refs/heads/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md
  ```

- Detailed docs: [docs/README.opencode.md](docs/README.opencode.md)

### Pi

Install Superpowers as a Pi package from this repository:

```bash
pi install git:github.com/obra/superpowers
```

For local development, run Pi with this checkout loaded as a temporary package:

```bash
pi -e /path/to/superpowers
```

The Pi package loads the Superpowers skills and a small extension that injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and again after compaction. Pi has native skills, so no compatibility `Skill` tool is required. Subagent and task-list tools remain optional Pi companion packages.

### Qwen Code

Qwen Code installs plugins from Claude Code marketplaces directly.

- Install the plugin from this repository, and pick `superpowers` when prompted:

  ```bash
  qwen extensions install obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  qwen extensions update superpowers
  ```

### Hermes Agent

Install Superpowers as a Hermes plugin from this repository:

```bash
hermes plugins install obra/superpowers --enable
```

Restart any active Hermes sessions after installing. Note: Hermes has no
post-compaction hook, so a very long session that compacts over its first
turn loses the bootstrap — start a fresh session if skills stop triggering.

### Muse

Superpowers is available as a native Muse plugin — same repo, same skills, all harnesses. The `using-superpowers` bootstrap is injected via the native `SessionStart` hook alongside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi, and the rest — no per-session opt-in.

- Install from a local checkout:

  ```bash
  muse plugins install ./
  muse plugins approve superpowers
  ```

  Or clone and install:

  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
  muse plugins install ./superpowers
  muse plugins approve superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  muse plugins update superpowers
  ```

Restart any active Muse sessions after installing so the `SessionStart` hook takes effect — skills are active immediately, hooks require approval on first install. To verify, start a fresh session and send `Let's make a react todo list` — a working install auto-triggers `brainstorming` before any code is written. Version is tracked in `.version-bump.json` so `scripts/bump-version.sh` keeps it in sync.

## The Basic Workflow

1. **brainstorming** - Activates before building anything. Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it, then plays its understanding back for correction. Small changes get agreed in chat; projects get a written design document a builder could plan from.

2. **using-git-worktrees** - Activates after design approval. Creates isolated workspace on new branch, runs project setup, verifies clean test baseline.

3. **writing-plans** - Activates with approved design. Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.

4. **subagent-driven-development** or **executing-plans** - Activates with plan. Either dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough), or implements every task inline in the current session with one fresh review of the whole branch at the end (cheapest).

5. **test-driven-development** - Activates during implementation. Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit. Deletes code written before tests.

6. **requesting-code-review** - Activates between tasks. Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.

7. **finishing-a-development-branch** - Activates when tasks complete. Verifies tests, presents options (merge/PR/keep/discard), cleans up worktree.

**The agent checks for relevant skills before any task.** Mandatory workflows, not suggestions.

## When Something Goes Wrong

Sometimes a session misbehaves: a skill fires when it shouldn't, stays silent when it should, or the agent ignores its plan, repeats work, or burns more tokens than you'd expect. Ask your coding agent to "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session" and it will invoke the **diagnosing-superpowers** skill. To examine an earlier session, name it: "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in session `<id>`".

The skill reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and, if you want, packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

## Community

Superpowers is built by [Jesse Vincent](https://blog.fsck.com) and the rest of the folks at [Prime Radiant](https://primeradiant.com).

- **Discord**: [Join us](https://discord.gg/35wsABTejz) for community support, questions, and sharing what you're building with Superpowers
- **Issues**: https://github.com/obra/superpowers/issues
- **Release announcements**: [Sign up](https://primeradiant.com/superpowers/) to get notified about new versions

## What's Inside

### Skills Library

**Testing**
- **test-driven-development** - RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle (includes testing anti-patterns reference)

**Debugging**
- **systematic-debugging** - 4-phase root cause process (includes root-cause-tracing, defense-in-depth, condition-based-waiting techniques)
- **verification-before-completion** - Ensure it's actually fixed
- **diagnosing-superpowers** - Work out what went wrong in a session, with evidence; export a scrubbed bundle or file an issue

**Collaboration** 
- **brainstorming** - Drawing out intent before building
- **writing-plans** - Detailed implementation plans
- **executing-plans** - Inline plan execution: one context, one final review
- **dispatching-parallel-agents** - Concurrent subagent workflows
- **requesting-code-review** - Pre-review checklist
- **receiving-code-review** - Responding to feedback
- **using-git-worktrees** - Parallel development branches
- **finishing-a-development-branch** - Merge/PR decision workflow
- **subagent-driven-development** - Fast iteration with two-stage review (spec compliance, then code quality)

**Meta**
- **writing-skills** - Create new skills following best practices (includes testing methodology)
- **using-superpowers** - Introduction to the skills system

## Philosophy

- **Test-Driven Development** - Write tests first, always
- **Systematic over ad-hoc** - Process over guessing
- **Complexity reduction** - Simplicity as primary goal
- **Evidence over claims** - Verify before declaring success

Read [the original release announcement](https://blog.fsck.com/2025/10/09/superpowers/).

## Contributing

The general contribution process for Superpowers is below. Keep in mind that we don't generally accept contributions of new skills and that any updates to skills must work across all of the coding agents we support.

1. Fork the repository
2. Switch to the 'dev' branch
3. Create a branch for your work
4. Follow the `writing-skills` skill for creating and testing new and modified skills
5. Submit a PR, being sure to fill in the pull request template.

Skill-behavior tests use the drill eval harness from [superpowers-evals](https://github.com/prime-radiant-inc/superpowers-evals/), cloned into `evals/` — see `evals/README.md` for setup. Plugin-infrastructure tests live at `tests/` and run via the relevant `run-*.sh` or `npm test`.

See `skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md` for the complete guide.

## Updating

Superpowers updates are somewhat coding-agent dependent, but are often automatic.

## License

MIT License - see LICENSE file for details

## Visual companion telemetry

Because skills and plugins don't provide any feedback to creators, we have no idea how many of you are using Superpowers. By default, the Prime Radiant logo on brainstorming's optional visual companion feature is loaded from our website. It includes the version of Superpowers in use. It does not include any details about your project, prompt, or coding agent. We don't see your clicks or anything about what you're building. This helps us have a rough idea of how many folks are using Superpowers and which version of Superpowers they're using. It's 100% optional. To disable this, set the environment variable `SUPERPOWERS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY` to any true value. Superpowers also honors Claude Code's `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` opt-outs.

repos.readme_excerpt:
# ESP32 iPhone Agent **Let an AI model use a real iPhone — with a $7 ESP32. No Mac, no developer account, no jailbreak.** English · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) Demo video and updates: [X @iamhenryyuan](https://x.com/iamhenryyuan) · [YouTube demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ly4im-P4jYg) [![CI](https://github.com/onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue) ![Board](https://img.shields.io/badge/board-ESP32--S3-red)

**Example 1 — draw on a canvas.** *"Open Whiteboard and draw a smiley face"*: the agent searches for the app, opens it and draws the face with continuous strokes. Every step's screenshot, with its tap or stroke drawn on top, stays on the step wall.

**Example 2 — set an alarm.** *"Set an alarm for 7:00 AM that repeats every day, then save it"*: the agent opens Clock, types 0700 into the time wheel, ticks the days under Repeat several taps at a time, and saves. Left: the real iPhone with the ESP32 plugged in; right: the web UI. The agent sees the phone through AirPlay screen mirroring and touches it through a tiny ESP32-S3 board that plugs into the phone's USB port as a mouse and keyboard. Any OpenAI-compatible vision model can be the brain — a cloud API, or a model you run yourself. ## Why Most iPhone automation drives the phone through XCTest / WebDriverAgent. That needs a Mac, Xcode, a signed helper app and an Apple developer account (a free account's signature expires every 7 days). This project uses the same paths a person uses — the screen and a pointer — so the phone needs nothing installed. | | ESP32 iPhone Agent | XCTest / WebDriverAgent tools | |----------------------------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------| | Apple developer account | **Not needed** | Needed (to sign the runner) | | Xcode | **Not needed** | Needed | | Computer | Mac **or Linux** | Mac | | App installed on the phone | **None** | Test runner app | | Jailbreak | Not needed | Not needed | | Extra hardware | ESP32-S3 board (~$7) | USB cable | | Works in any app, incl. games | Yes (it only sees pixels) | Mostly (depends on the accessibility tree) | ## How it works - **Eyes — AirPlay mirroring.** The phone mirrors its screen to [UxPlay](https://github.com/FDH2/UxPlay) running on your computer; a GStreamer pipeline turns the stream into JPEG frames for the agent and the web page. - **Hands — a USB HID bridge.** An ESP32-S3 plugged into the phone shows up as a standard USB mouse and keyboard. With iOS AssistiveTouch on, the mouse moves an on-screen pointer, so a click is a tap and a drag is a swipe. The board connects to the computer over Wi-Fi and executes simple line commands (`move`, `click`, `type`, …); all logic stays on the computer. - **Brain — a planner and an actor.** A planner model writes a short plan from the goal and the current screen. An actor model then looks at each new screenshot and picks the next action: tap, swipe, draw a path, type, press a key, go home, or finish. Both roles can be the same model. - **Closing the loop.** The pointer is relative, so the server tracks where it is. Before each tap it wiggles the pointer, finds it on the mirrored screen and corrects any miss, refining the calibration as it goes. After each action it checks whether the screen actually changed and tells the model, so a missed tap is noticed and retried instead of built upon. Repeated actions trigger a re-plan; a dropped link or a bad reply is recovered from. ## Hardware | Part | Notes | |---|---| | **ESP32-S3 board** | Tested with a [Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_esp32s3_getting_started/), plain version without pre-soldered headers (not the Sense camera version, not the Plus). About $7 from Seeed, or about ¥40-50 on Taobao in China (search "XIAO ESP32S3"). Any ESP32-S3 board whose USB-C port is wired to the S3's native USB works. | | **iPhone** | USB-C models plug in directly. Lightning models need a Lightning to USB Camera Adapter. The phone powers the board. | | **Computer** | macOS or Linux, on the same network as the phone; runs UxPlay and the server. | | **Vision model** | Any OpenAI-compatible chat API that accepts images. Running a model locally is optional. |

Use a USB-C hub with power pass-through if the phone should keep charging while the board is plugged in. ## Quick start > **Set up with an AI coding agent.** Paste this into Claude Code, Codex or a similar agent on the computer the > board will connect to: > > ```text > Clone https://github.com/onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent and follow its README to set it up on this machine: > flash the ESP32-S3 plugged in over USB, install UxPlay and the server, write server/.env for my model API, start > the server and give me the web UI address. Ask me for the Wi-Fi name/password and the model API key. > ``` ### 1. Flash the board Install [arduino-cli](https://arduino.github.io/arduino-cli/) and the ESP32 core (3.x), then: ```bash cp hardware/hid_bridge/secrets.example.h hardware/hid_bridge/secrets.h # edit secrets.h: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi name/password and the IP address of the computer running the server hardware/flash.sh # optional arguments: [serial port] [--debug] ``` ### 2. Install and start the server ```bash # UxPlay — macOS: brew install uxplay # UxPlay — Debian / Ubuntu: sudo apt install uxplay gstreamer1.0-plugins-good gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad gstreamer1.0-libav cd server python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e . cp .env.example .env # set LLM_BASE_URL / LLM_MODEL / LLM_API_KEY set -a && . ./.env && set +a && .venv/bin/python -m hidagent ``` Open `http://:8890` in a browser. ### 3. Set up the phone (once) 1. **Settings → Accessibility → Touch → AssistiveTouch**: turn it on. 2. Plug the board into the phone. A round pointer appears; the web page shows *controller connected*. 3. **Control Center → Screen Mirroring → iPhone Agent**. The live screen appears in the web page. 4. In the web page, open **Manual controls → Calibrate**. The server moves the pointer, finds it on the live screen and calibrates itself in a few seconds; if it cannot see the pointer, it asks you to click exactly on it. ### 4. Give it a task Type a goal (for example *"Open Settings and go to Wi-Fi"*) and press **Start**, or click one of the examples. ## Web UI - **Live phone** — click to tap, drag to swipe, scroll to scroll; manual Home, Back, typing and keys. - **Live log** — every plan, thought and action as it happens, with timings. - **Step wall** — the screenshot the model decided on for every step, with its tap or swipe drawn on top, plus the model's reasoning and how long thinking and acting took. Click a card to zoom in. - **Taps** are marked with a red ring and a spreading ripple, swipes and strokes with a yellow path; the **Motion** switch turns the animation off. Taps the model marked `precise` (pointer checked before tapping) are labelled in the log. - **Emergency stop** (or Esc) stops the agent and releases the pointer. **Clear history** empties the log. - English and Simplified Chinese interface. ## Configuration Set in `server/.env` (see [`.env.example`](server/.env.example)): | Variable | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `LLM_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/v1` | OpenAI-compatible endpoint | | `LLM_MODEL` / `LLM_API_KEY` | — | Model name and API key | | `LLM_EXTRA_BODY` | `{}` | JSON merged into every request (e.g. to turn off a model's thinking mode) | | `LLM_TOKEN_PARAM` | `auto` | Token-limit field: `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` (newer OpenAI models), or `auto` to detect | | `ACTOR_*` / `PLANNER_*` | — | Per-role overrides of any `LLM_*` variable | | `AIRPLAY_NAME` | `iPhone Agent` | Receiver name in the phone's Screen Mirroring list | | `PORT` / `DEVICE_PORT` | `8890` / `7300` | Web UI port / port the board connects to | | `HIDAGENT_DATA` | `~/.hidagent` | Calibration and debug traces | | `HIDAGENT_DEBUG` | `0` | Debug mode, see below | ### Local model (optional) A cloud API is enough. If you want everything on your own hardware, this is the setup the project was developed and timed with: - Model: [nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) - Serving: [Qwen3.8-Flash-Dual-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold](https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Dual-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold) — two NVIDIA DGX Sparks with tensor parallelism (TP=2), OpenAI-compatible API - Speed: about 1.3 s per action and 2 s per plan, with thinking mode off: ```bash LLM_BASE_URL=http://:8888/v1 LLM_MODEL=Qwen3.8-Flash-Next LLM_EXTRA_BODY='{"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}' ``` Any other OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, …) with a vision model works the same way. ## Debug mode Set `HIDAGENT_DEBUG=1` to log every board command with its latency and to save one folder per agent run: ``` ~/.hidagent/traces/20261012-005207/ ├── steps.jsonl # every model call (prompt, raw reply, latency) and every action ├── 002.jpg # the screenshot each model call saw └── ... ``` `hardware/flash.sh --debug` builds firmware that echoes each command and its duration over USB serial. ## Board protocol The board holds no logic. On connecting it sends `hello `; then the server sends one command per line over TCP and the board answers `ok` or `err `. | Command | Effect | |---|---| | `ping` | Health check | | `home` | Push the pointer into the top-left corner (a known position) | | `move ` | Relative pointer move, at a constant pace so iOS pointer acceleration stays predictable | | `press` / `release` / `click` | Left button down / up / both | | `scroll ` | Scroll wheel | | `type ` | Type ASCII text | | `key ` | Press keys, e.g. `enter`, `cmd+h`, `cmd+space` | If the Wi-Fi link drops, the board releases all buttons and reconnects on its own. While the phone is locked, its USB port sleeps: the board then tries to wake it and otherwise answers `err phone usb asleep` instead of waiting. A watchdog restarts the board if it ever stops responding. ## Project layout ``` hardware/ ESP32-S3 firmware (Arduino) and flash script server/ agent, web UI, screen capture and board link (Python, FastAPI) serve/: optional minimal server to host a Hugging Face vision model yourself ``` ## Roadmap - [ ] Test a fully local setup with DiffusionGemma (`server/serve/` has an experimental OpenAI-compatible server) - [ ] Landscape apps (screen coordinates and calibration assume portrait) - [ ] Non-ASCII text input (e.g. Chinese through the iOS pinyin keyboard) - [ ] More example tasks across popular apps ### Exploring: drop the computer Right now the board is just the hands. The brain and the eyes run on a separate computer. The next idea is to drop the computer. Swap the ESP32 for a small board that can run Linux, and run the whole loop on it: see the screen, decide, tap. The phone would only need that one board, which you could carry in your pocket. The board could talk to the phone over USB or Bluetooth, and call a local or cloud model. These are directions, not promises. If you're interested, or you've tried something similar, open an issue. ## Limitations - iOS does not mirror some screens (passcode entry, Apple Pay, DRM video); the agent cannot see them. - Mirroring stops when the phone locks; keep auto-lock off while the agent works. - Keyboard input is ASCII only. - Re-calibrate after changing AssistiveTouch tracking speed. - Landscape apps are not supported yet: drawings and taps there land in the wrong place. - On Linux machines with several network interfaces, limit Avahi (mDNS) to the interface on the phone's network if the phone does not list the receiver. ## Responsible use Only automate devices and accounts you own or are allowed to use, and respect the terms of the apps involved. The agent acts with your hands: watch it, and keep the emergency stop within reach. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Run the checks before sending a change: ```bash cd server && pip install -e ".[dev]" && ruff check . && pytest ``` ## Related projects Other ways people drive an iPhone with code or AI, and how this project differs. Corrections welcome. | Project | Approach | Needs on the phone / host | Difference from this project | |---|---|---|---| | [VersaiOS](https://github.com/zhaodashuaibi/VersaiOS) | UxPlay mirroring + ESP32-S3 Bluetooth mouse + vision model | ESP32 tethered to a computer over USB serial; desktop GUI, mainly Windows | Closest in spirit. One tap per instruction, no planning step or before/after screen check | | [ja1chen/actell](https://github.com/ja1chen/actell) | Agent app on the iPhone, screenshots and taps via Apple's CoreDevice debug channel | Developer Mode, pairing + Developer Disk Image, Xcode self-signing | This project needs no Developer Mode, no app on the phone and no signing | | [AidenAI-IO/aiden-firmware](https://github.com/AidenAI-IO/aiden-firmware) | Dedicated board: HDMI capture + USB keyboard/mouse + multimodal model | HDMI capture chip and dock; mainly Android | Uses AirPlay instead of HDMI capture, so no capture hardware | | [yoyicue/glassbox](https://github.com/yoyicue/glassbox) | PicoKVM HDMI capture + USB HID, observe/decide/act/verify loop | macOS controller and PicoKVM | Runs on Linux with a single ESP32 | | [boboabw/phone-agent](https://github.com/boboabw/phone-agent) | ESP32-S3 Bluetooth HID + AssistiveTouch, agent runs as an iPhone app | Mac + Xcode to build and sign the app | Nothing to install on the phone | | [dovydaskel/Iphone-control-for-social-media](https://github.com/dovydaskel/Iphone-control-for-social-media) | ESP32 Bluetooth mouse with OpenCV pointer correction, scripted posting | Mac | Similar closed-loop pointer idea; this project adds a vision-model planner/executor | | [VKCOM/devicehub](https://github.com/VKCOM/devicehub) | ESP32 Bluetooth mouse for iOS device farms | Farm infrastructure | Device-farm tooling, no AI agent | | [NolanCotter/AirBridge](https://github.com/NolanCotter/AirBridge) / [gbulog/pcairplay](https://github.com/gbulog/pcairplay) | UxPlay on Linux + the PC's own Bluetooth as keyboard/mouse | Linux PC with Bluetooth | Manual remote control, no AI | Other routes: WebDriverAgent/XCUITest-based tools such as [mobile-mcp](https://github.com/mobile-next/mobile-mcp) and [Midscene](https://github.com/web-infra-dev/midscene) need a Mac and code signing; tools built on macOS iPhone Mirroring need a Mac. ## Acknowledgements [UxPlay](https://github.com/FDH2/UxPlay) (AirPlay receiver) · [Arduino ESP32 core](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32) and [TinyUSB](https://github.com/hathach/tinyusb) (USB HID) · [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

repos.name: d2r-mobile
repos.description: Open-source iOS / macOS compatibility layer for Diablo II: Resurrected with the Reign of the Warlock expansion. Runs your own Switch copy natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac — full touch controls, 60 fps, new endgame modes. Bring your own game files. 开源的《暗黑破坏神 II：狱火重生》术士君临 iOS / macOS 兼容层
repos.readme_excerpt:
# D2R Mobile **An open-source iOS / macOS compatibility layer for Diablo II: Resurrected with the Reign of the Warlock expansion.** It brings the Nintendo Switch release you bought, expansion included, to iPhone, iPad and Mac in full: the original game code runs natively, every control is rebuilt for touch, the frame rate holds at 60 fps, and you are in a game one second after the main menu. There is now a native macOS version as well (first version): on an Apple silicon Mac it starts on double-click and works with keyboard, mouse and gamepad. This is not a tech demo that "sort of runs". It is a mobile version polished for daily play, from your first character all the way through the endgame. Platforms: iPhone / iPad (iOS 26 and later; iOS 18 – 25 with the older-API build) · Mac (Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later; macOS 15 – 25 with the older-API build) · Game version: Switch release with Reign of the Warlock, 1.0.34.0 (corresponds to PC version 3.3.94012) · English / 中文 · License: MIT · **Bring your own game files** 中文: [README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md)

| 100% | 60 fps | about 1 s | about 3.8 W | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | The original gameplay, because it is the original program | Steady, with no drops once the device warms up | From the main menu into a game | Whole-device power draw at 60 fps | ## What it is, and what it is not **It is:** - The game's own aarch64 program, **executing directly on the device**, with no emulated CPU. iPhone and Switch use the same class of processor; only the handful of instructions that cannot run unchanged under Apple's kernel are rewritten, and every other byte of the program is left exactly as shipped. Every class, every Runeword, Terror Zones, bosses, drop rules and quest flow are identical to the original. - The platform services the game expects — system calls, the file system, the graphics API, audio, input — provided by a small host written for Apple platforms. The graphics API is reimplemented entirely on Apple's Metal with no emulation layer in between, and the shaders are translated offline from the game's originals. - A port built for phones, and taken all the way: a complete touch control scheme, edge-to-edge iPhone and true full-screen iPad display, controller support, a power saver mode, save sync, English and Chinese, and a whole set of endgame modes and quality-of-life features the original never had. **It is not:** - An emulator, cloud gaming, or streaming. - **A source of game content. It contains none and distributes none.** There is no game program, art, text, data table or shader in this repository; all of that is generated on your own machine from your own files (see [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md)). What the repository does carry is the interface information we recorded to make the port work — shader interface descriptions, the graphics API function table, addresses inside the program and the like — listed item by item in [docs/DERIVED.md](docs/DERIVED.md). - Online. There is no multiplayer; the game runs fully offline and needs no online account. ## Battle-tested All **44** iPhones and iPads in the closed beta — 35 devices registered for direct install (25 iPhones and 10 iPads), plus 9 TestFlight accounts with one device each — **completed Normal, Nightmare and Hell with multiple characters**, and the experience was excellent. From an iPhone 14 Pro Max with 6 GB of memory to the latest iPad Pro, not one device fell behind. | | Models | |---|---| | iPhone | 14 Pro Max, 15, 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 17 Pro Max and more | | iPad | iPad Air, iPad mini, iPad Pro 11-inch and 12.9 / 13-inch (including M2 and M4) and more | | Lowest model tested | **iPhone 14 Pro Max (A16, 6 GB): a flawless 60 fps** | iPhone and iPad share a single install package.

## Fast, smooth, and easy on the battery Measured on a real device (iPhone 17 Pro Max): | Item | Reading | |---|---| | In-game frame rate | **60 fps**, steady, with no drops once the device warms up | | App launch | 0.15 s | | To the main menu | about 1 s | | From the main menu into a game | **about 1 s** | | Quick Restart, back in a game | about 1.2 s | | Longest frame when changing acts | about 0.1 s | | Whole-device power, 60 fps | **about 3.8 W** (in camp, 50% brightness): nearly 5 hours of continuous play on a full charge | | Whole-device power, power saver mode at 30 fps | **about 1.85 W**, about half the 60 fps figure, for about twice the battery life | Measurement conditions: power is whole-device power measured on 2026-10-10 on an iPhone 17 Pro Max, standing in the Act I camp at 50% brightness, with 60 fps and power saver mode measured in the same scene; battery life is calculated from the measured power and the battery capacity, not by playing from full to empty. Launch and game-entry times were measured on the same model in 2026-10; frame rate and act-change readings were taken on the same model on 2026-10-12 while moving through areas and changing acts after entering a game. The install package is only a little over 100 MB. The game resources (about 5.6 GB) are placed on the phone separately, and updating the app touches neither your saves nor the resources. Why it is this fast: the program executes natively, and not a single instruction goes through emulation; graphics go straight to Metal; every shader is translated offline and compiled ahead of time, so nothing is compiled when you enter a new scene. Older chips (A16 and earlier, such as the iPhone 14 family and iPhone 15) do not support the game's original compressed texture format; they need an extra texture pack made from your own game files, and then run at full frame rate too — see [docs/LEGACY_DEVICES.md](docs/LEGACY_DEVICES.md). ## Redesigned for fingers This is not a gamepad pasted onto the screen. Every panel and every action was rebuilt for fingers under one design principle: **keep the original interface language, and use gestures instead of adding buttons to the screen**. Text sizes and tap targets are sized for fingers. You know how to play the moment you pick it up, and it stays comfortable over long sessions.

- **Move**: a virtual stick with precise diagonals; tap an NPC or the ground to path there automatically; doors, portals and cave entrances are tappable across their whole surface. - **Fight**: press a skill button to cast, hold to keep casting, **drag to aim at any angle**; nearby monsters are targeted automatically. Two skill sets. Skills on your secondary weapons cast with one tap — the game swaps weapons, casts, and swaps back — and the button shows the charges remaining. - **Boss health bar**: pinned to the top of the screen, showing the percentage remaining. - **Items**: tap, double-tap, long-press and drag and drop all track your finger. Double-tap gear to equip or unequip it; drag an item anywhere onto the vendor panel to sell it; on a stack, double-tap takes 1 and long-press takes 3; long-press an empty inventory slot to sort everything. - **Text**: typed with the system keyboard. Character names can be in Chinese; leave the name blank for a random one. - **Screen**: on iPhone the 19.5:9 display is filled edge to edge, clear of the notch and rounded corners; on iPad the game fills the entire screen, and the interface centers itself when you open a panel; the 3D picture can be brightened. ### Controller Connect a controller and press any button: the interface switches to the original controller layout, with button prompts at the bottom of every panel. Touch the screen and you are back in the touch interface instantly. Inventory, stash, skill tree, Chronicle and settings are fully controller-navigable, with the same button mapping as on Switch.

## New ways to play, on top of the original Finishing the original game is only the beginning. Without touching the original rules, we added a full set of endgame content that keeps you farming. ### Greater Rift Enter through the red portal in Harrogath after completing Hell. There are 100 levels, and the monsters grow stronger with each one; fill the progress bar and slay the Rift Guardian within 15 minutes to clear a level. Every 2 levels cleared grants +1 Skill Point and +5 Stat Points, and the skill level cap rises from 20 to 40. Every 10 levels has a first-clear reward, and clearing level 10 unlocks six new equipment slots for your mercenary.

### Endgame Boss Rush, Elysium mode, and the Kill Board - **Endgame Boss Rush**: unlocks after completing Hell, with 12 stages; stage 11 is Diablo Clone, and stage 12 is the three Uber bosses. - **Elysium mode** (chosen at character creation): Unique ×5, Set ×3, Runes ×5; the "no drop" chance is cut to a tenth, and bosses always drop as on a first kill. - **Kill Board**: for every boss, the number of kills, the time of the first kill, how many Unique and Set items it has dropped, and your best and average kill times.

### Storage: a collector's paradise - **Chronicle stash**: every identified Unique and Set item has its own fixed slot, shared by all characters, searchable, with deposit and withdraw; the Deposit button sends the Unique and Set items in your inventory and Horadric Cube there in one tap. - **Stash**: widened to 14 columns, with 5 personal pages and 5 shared pages. - **Trove**: the gem, rune and material pages merged into one, with the Horadric Cube's crafting grid in the middle, so finding things and crafting no longer means flipping between pages. Runes, gems and materials you put into the personal or shared pages are filed here automatically. - **Pouch**: an extended inventory. Runes and gems found in the field go into it automatically and take up no inventory space.

### Effortless farming | | | |---|---| | Auto-recast buffs | Buff skills you have learned do not need a slot on the skill bar: when a buff runs out, it is recast the moment you stand still; buffs that come from your secondary weapons (such as Battle Orders from Call to Arms) swap weapons, recast and swap back on their own | | Potions and belt | Auto-drink has two tiers: a healing potion below 50% Life, a rejuvenation potion below 30%; **your mercenary is fed automatically by the same rule**. Potions on the ground are picked up automatically when the belt has room; double-tap an empty belt slot to refill the whole belt | | Loot filter | From Nightmare on, the original loot filter is switched on automatically to hide clutter: light filtering in Nightmare, heavy in Hell | | Auto-pickup | Low runes and gems go straight into the Pouch; the high ones are left for you to pick up yourself | | Valuable drop alerts | High runes and Unique items raise a light beam and land with a different drop sound; the phone vibrates at one of three strengths — light, medium or heavy — according to value | | Runeword helper | Long-press a socketed base to list the Runewords it can make and their stats; once you have the runes, socket them all in one tap | | Minimap guidance | Every map marks its Waypoint and exits; every quest goal is on the map; when a target is off screen, its name is written along the screen edge | | Chores removed | Free identification, free Town Portal with no scrolls needed, spawning right beside the Waypoint, Quick Restart, refreshable vendor stock | | Saves | Saved immediately when you switch apps, swipe the app away or quit; iCloud sync across devices (requires signing with a paid developer account) | Most features can be toggled one by one in game under Options → Custom.

### English and Chinese The whole game switches between English and Chinese under Options → Custom; after a restart, both the interface and the voice acting are in the language you chose. In English, items, skills and monsters use the original Diablo II wording, and everything we added — Greater Rift, Chronicle, the settings page, controller prompts — is in English too.

## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR G["Your game files
(program + resources)"] --> P["Rewriter
changes only a few instructions"] G --> S["Shader translation
original → Metal"] P --> H["Host
system services"] S --> X["Graphics layer
the graphics API on Metal"] H --> A["iOS app
touch and interface"] X --> A ``` | Part | Where | What it does | |---|---|---| | Program rewriter | `dm/tools/patch_nso.py` | Rewrites only the few instructions that cannot run unchanged under Apple's kernel (thread-pointer registers, system calls, timers) and leaves the rest of the program byte-for-byte as shipped | | Host | `dm/host` | Loads the rewritten program and provides the platform services it calls | | Graphics | `dm/gfx` | Implements the game's graphics API on Metal; shaders are translated offline from the game's originals | | iOS app | `dm/ios` | The app shell, touch controls and interface | | Verification | `dm/verify` | Checks that the rewritten code behaves exactly like the original, plus the regression gates every change goes through | **Why you can trust it:** the stability is not luck. The test and verification tooling is part of the project — unit tests for the host and graphics layers, an equivalence check for every rewritten instruction, scripted walkthrough regression for the touch interface, and on-device smoke tests. Start with `make -C dm/host/tests run`, `make -C dm/gfx/tests run` and `dm/verify/regress.sh` (run them inside the Python environment prepared in step 2 below; `regress.sh` also needs `brew install llvm`). How to contribute is in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Which devices are supported | Device | Playable? | How | How sure we are | |---|---|---|---| | **iPhone / iPad, A17 Pro and later** (iPhone 15 Pro and later, iPhone 16 and later, iPads with M-series chips) | Yes | iOS 26 or later: the default shell / default build; iOS 18 – 25: the iOS 18 shell / [older-API build](docs/OLDER_SYSTEMS.md) | Main devices, played daily | | **iPhone / iPad, A16 and earlier** (all iPhone 14 models, iPhone 15 / 15 Plus, iPhone 13 series and so on) | Yes, with one extra step | Make a Legacy Device Pack from your own game files as in [docs/LEGACY_DEVICES.md](docs/LEGACY_DEVICES.md) and include it when making the install package; the system split is the same as the row above | Played by players: iPhone 14 Pro Max (A16, 6 GB) at 60 fps; iPhone 13 Pro Max (A15, 6 GB) in the 30 fps mode | | **Chips older than A15, devices with 4 GB of RAM** | No reports yet | Same as the row above | If you have tried, please open an Issue and tell us | | **Mac, Apple silicon** | Yes (native macOS App) | macOS 26 or later: the default build; macOS 15 – 25: the [older-API build](docs/OLDER_SYSTEMS.md). Keyboard, mouse and gamepad all work; what each can do is in [docs/MAC.md](docs/MAC.md) | A player has played the older-API build on macOS 15.7.7 | | **Intel Macs** | Not supported | — | — | **What the dialogs in the App mean** - **"One More Step for This Device"**: this phone can run the game; the install package was made without the Legacy Device Pack. Make the pack as in [docs/LEGACY_DEVICES.md](docs/LEGACY_DEVICES.md), make the install package again with it and reinstall. - **"Device Not Supported … iPhone 15 Pro and later can play"**: this is the old text from before v1.0.9. You are on an old version; update to the latest. For A16 and earlier devices, then follow the line above. **What a package you build yourself does not have, compared with our test-group builds**: the public version can be built and installed with a free Apple ID. Three things in our test-group builds are not in it: iCloud save sync (the App needs the iCloud signing entitlement, which a self-signed package does not have), downloading packs and resources inside the App, and new-version notices (these two use our own server). The game itself and the features we added are the same. ## Getting started Both routes start with **the files of the game you bought**: the Switch release of Diablo II: Resurrected plus the Reign of the Warlock expansion, updated to 1.0.34.0 (the version the console shows; it corresponds to PC version 3.3.94012, and the directory names and tools in this repository use the latter number). This project is built for the version with that expansion; using it without the expansion is not supported and has not been verified. How to prepare them is in [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md). This project is implemented and verified on the Switch release 1.0.34.0 (which corresponds to PC version 3.3.94012), and by default the tools accept only that version. Community users have reported adapting other versions on their own by following the structure of this repository, and running them successfully. The rule tables are grouped by game version (in `dm/tools/patch_nso.py`, keyed by the build ID of the main program); you are welcome to contribute the version you adapted. **Check your device first**: the "Which devices are supported" table above tells you which build to use and whether you also need a Legacy Device Pack. | | With a Mac | Without a Mac | |---|---|---| | Computer | An Apple silicon Mac with Xcode installed | Windows / Linux / a Mac without Xcode | | Method | A full build from source | Download a "shell" with no game content, use the packaging tool to add your own game content, then install it with a sideloading tool | | Status | The main route; everything above comes from it | Works end to end on Windows, from making the package to playing on a device, and the game program produced on the two systems is byte-for-byte identical; the one step nobody has tried yet is signing with a sideloading tool — try it and tell us | | Instructions | The three steps below | [docs/NO_XCODE.md](docs/NO_XCODE.md) | The Apple account used for signing: a paid developer account gives you everything; a free Apple ID works too (no iCloud save sync, and the app has to be re-signed and reinstalled every 7 days). The full list of dependencies is in [docs/DEPENDENCIES.md](docs/DEPENDENCIES.md). ### With a Mac: three steps 1. Put your game files in the workspace (default `~/dm-work`, or set `DM_ROOT`): ``` ~/dm-work/data/switch/3.3.94012/Update/ExeFS/ main, sdk, subsdk0 ~/dm-work/data/switch/3.3.94012/Update/RomFS/ data/… ``` 2. Prepare the workspace. This checks your tools, rewrites the game program, and translates the game's shaders to Metal. The first run takes a while; later runs skip what is already done. ``` ./setup.sh source ~/dm-work/build/cache/dm/venv/bin/activate # run everything after this inside the Python environment setup prepared; if you changed DM_ROOT, use it in place of ~/dm-work ``` 3. Fill in your signing details and build the app: ``` cp dm/ios/local.env.example dm/ios/local.env # set DM_TEAM_ID and DM_BUNDLE_ID; with a free Apple ID also set DM_FREE_ACCOUNT=1 and DM_IOS_UDID, and keep the phone connected while building cd dm/ios && ./run.sh build # targets both iPhone and iPad by default; for iPhone only: DM_DEVICE_FAMILY=1 ./run.sh build ``` The first time you open the app on your phone, it asks for the "game resource folder" — the 18 resource archives from your game files. Where to put them is in the section "The "game resource folder" that goes on the phone" of [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md). `./setup.sh check` is a health check: it reports the state of this computer, the tools, the game files and the signing configuration item by item, and for everything missing it says where to get it and which command to run next; it changes nothing. If what you have is a whole game package (`.xci` / `.nsp`), `./setup.sh ` first extracts the game files into place and then carries on (install hactool first). Run `./setup.sh` again after every update to a new commit: it rebuilds the patched binaries and the shader library for the current sources (steps that are already up to date are skipped). It also rewrites three files in the repository that change with your local tool fingerprints (`dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_chain.lock`, `dm/gfx/nvn/dmsh_chain.h`, `dm/gfx/nvn/c1_full.tsv`); that is expected, do not commit them. ### Playing directly on a Mac After the same `./setup.sh`, one more command builds a native macOS App that starts on double-click and works with keyboard, mouse and gamepad, with no developer account: ```bash source ~/dm-work/build/cache/dm/venv/bin/activate dm/tools/mac_app.sh # macOS 26 or later: produces ~/dm-work/out/macapp/D2R Mobile.app DM_MAC_M3=1 dm/tools/mac_app.sh # macOS 15 – 25: produces D2R Mobile M3.app ``` The interface is the original's gamepad interface. Keyboard: Space confirms, Esc goes back, Return, the `=` key opens the menu / a new character, W A S D moves, and every other gamepad button has a key. Mouse: clicking a monster, NPC or object walks over and interacts, and the skill slots, potion cells and key hints at the bottom, buttons and tabs in panels, the class figures when creating a character and the minimap can all be clicked; clicking empty ground walks there and holding keeps walking, clicking a monster attacks it, and items take double clicks and drags. With a keyboard, the prompts on screen show keyboard keys. Saves stay on this Mac (an App you build yourself

repos.name: CCBaga
repos.readme_excerpt:
CCBaga

A native macOS, Linux and Windows toolkit for a cleaner workspace and an environment you can verify.

Claude identities · Browser fingerprints · System settings · Network Skill

Features · Installation · Updates · Quick start · Usage guide · Architecture · Development · Contributing

![CCBaga: native control, observable environments](docs/readme-hero.png) **Intended use:** CCBaga is intended solely for people residing or traveling abroad to manage their own Claude identities. Use that violates Anthropic's official terms of service is prohibited. CCBaga brings local maintenance and environment setup into one focused desktop workflow. Inspect Claude data before removing it, rotate your companion browser's fingerprint and restart it, align system settings with a selected region, and compare real browser readings with the machine and network exit. Two applications work together: **CCBaga-A** owns native operations; **CCBaga-B** runs an isolated Fingerprint Chromium profile. Browser measurements return to the host through a local session. Changing a setting and verifying its effect are separate steps. ## Features
Local Claude identities

Archive the current local identity, switch to a saved identity or start with an empty workspace. Choose what stays shared and what moves with each identity.		 Fingerprint & restart

Generate a fresh seed, apply the selected region's language and timezone, then restart the companion browser.		 Real environment checks

Compare browser and machine readings with the actual network exit. Passing measured checks produces a green page and a large checkmark.
Native system settings

Apply timezone, preferred language and region settings. Open desktop controls for location and permissions; see platform-specific limits.		 AI-guided network setup

Three simple steps, a coding-agent selector and a copyable Skill installation prompt. Give the AI your files and connection details; it handles the commands.		 Claude Code CLI tools

Detect the installation method and version. Uninstall or reinstall through native, npm/bun, Homebrew or WinGet workflows.
**One region selector. Four everyday actions.** Easy setup puts browser cache cleanup, fingerprint rotation, timezone/language reset and identity archiving on the same page. The sidebar keeps advanced controls in Network, Claude identities, Browser and Computer. The interface supports **English and Chinese**, with shared YAML catalogs. Switching the interface language does not change the computer or browser language. The bilingual **Usage guide** covers common actions and data boundaries. See the [full guide](docs/usage.md). ## Installation **Platforms:** macOS 12 or later on Apple Silicon; Linux x86_64 with GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1; Windows 10/11 x86_64. Intel macOS and Linux ARM64 are not supported. Linux x86_64 packages include DEB, RPM, AppImage and Arch/pacman formats, with the companion browser included. See [Linux setup](docs/linux.md) for installation and platform limits. Official versions are published exclusively by the project owner, **liseami**. Windows x86_64 uses one NSIS setup installer containing both A and B. The installer is not Authenticode signed and may show SmartScreen; managed security policy can block it. See [Windows setup](docs/windows.md) for installation, toolchains and platform behaviors. ### macOS Download the official installer from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/liseami/CCBaga/releases/latest). The distribution package is named `CCBaga--macos-arm64.dmg`. It contains both applications: | Application | Installed bundle | Role | | --- | --- | --- | | CCBaga-A | `CCBaga-A.app` | Identity management, system settings and environment verification | | CCBaga-B | `CCBaga-B.app` | Companion browser with a dedicated profile | Download **one DMG**; it contains both applications. There is no separate browser download. The installer uses the same pixel-art style as this README. 1. Open the disk image and drag **both applications** into Applications. 2. Launch CCBaga-A. It starts the companion browser automatically. 3. Choose English at the bottom of the sidebar if needed. Source builds are available through the [development guide](#development). ## Updates Use **Check for updates** at the bottom of CCBaga-A’s sidebar. Startup checks quietly; installation only starts when you choose **Update and restart**. Downloads show actual progress and are verified before installation. Failed downloads can be retried; a failed restart does not download the update again. On **macOS**, in-app updates replace A; use the latest DMG to update both apps. On **Windows**, a verified NSIS update installs both A and B after closing this companion browser. On **Linux**, use the package manager or full package. ## Quick start ### Everyday setup Open **Easy setup**, select a country or region, then choose an action. Browser fingerprint rotation closes and restarts CCBaga-B, so save unfinished browser work first. Selecting a region changes language, timezone and regional settings; it does **not** change your public IP. ### Claude identities Open **Claude identities** to manage the local state of both Claude Code and Claude Desktop. Choose **Empty identity** to archive the current state before leaving a fresh workspace, or choose a saved identity to restore it. Every switch saves the outgoing identity first. Expand **Keep in workspace** to choose retention for skills and commands, plugins, MCP configuration, personal settings, project records, conversation history, and caches/logs. Login data always moves with an archived identity. Project source outside Claude's own data directories is not scanned. A confirmation names the outgoing identity and summarizes what stays in the workspace before closing recognized Claude processes. Portrait identity cards scroll horizontally with spring motion and subtle hover tilt. The white empty identity stays first, followed by the current local account with available name, email and organization information. **Archive** saves the current state and leaves an empty identity. Select a saved card to restore that identity. **Direct delete** removes selected current data without creating an archive; deleting a saved card removes only that archive. Both deletion actions require an explicit confirmation. A local SQLite database tracks names, policies and recovery state. Data is compressed into an authenticated, encrypted `.baga` container outside Claude's working directories. Archive verification precedes workspace changes; failed switches roll back, and an interrupted switch exposes recovery. Recovery also saves the pre-recovery state. Ordinary archive tools cannot open this container directly; filesystem ownership or administrator access is not an absolute secrecy boundary. Expired or revoked server-side logins may need authentication again. The app manages the default local directories, not every custom Claude profile. The program-maintenance controls uninstall or reinstall Claude Code without removing the identity vault. ### Browser verification Open **Browser** or the companion browser's local test page to measure the actual environment. Checks cover the network exit, country, timezone, language, platform, CPU count, engine version and location settings. The success page appears only when the measured checks match, the report reaches the cleaner and no measurement error remains. **DNS and WebRTC leak checks are not independently verified.** A green result describes the measured checks, not a guarantee of anonymity or account acceptance. ### Network setup Open **Network** for three steps: **Get VPS → Get residential proxy → Install Skill**. Select **General**, **Codex**, **Cursor**, **OpenCode** or **Copilot**, then copy the installation prompt into your local coding agent. The prompt follows the app's English/Chinese setting. The [Network Skill](skills/ccbaga-network/README.md#installation) follows the Agent Skills specification and installs separately from the apps. It supports the npm `skills` CLI: `npx skills add liseami/CCBaga --skill ccbaga-network --global`; the AI selects the target tool, uses copy mode on Windows, and disables installer tracking. Give the AI your VPS address, the three matching PEM/PPK/PUB files or downloaded key bundle, and your residential SOCKS5 connection details. It handles file paths, private configuration, commands and checks; you do not need to open a terminal or edit JSON. Missing resources are purchased by you with the AI's guidance. Remote setup runs only after approval of the actual server changes. The Skill supports authorized Debian 12/13 servers using root key login on port 22. It checks the SSH identity and fixed SOCKS5 exit, configures Xray/Reality and delivers a private local import file after server self-checks pass. Client setup uses **TUN ON**, **System Proxy OFF** and an empty explicit browser proxy; actual TUN/browser verification remains a separate step. The subscription URL uses HTTP and contains credentials; prefer the file retrieved over SSH. Provider buttons link to [DMIT](https://www.dmit.io/aff.php?aff=28800) and [Webshare](https://www.webshare.io/?referral_code=qlm1mt9xibc9). Network setup is optional; local cleanup does not require a VPS or a proxy subscription. **The app does not collect SSH keys or proxy credentials and does not deploy to servers.** ## Architecture ![Pixel architecture map: native core, companion browser and a separate AI Network Skill](docs/architecture.svg) The UI owns inputs and presentation. Rust owns validation, task locks, process identity checks and execution. Small Objective-C bridges call macOS APIs; Rust Linux and Windows boundaries use native process identity checks and platform controls. The browser test page has no Tauri command access; it exchanges context and measurements through a random-token loopback session. | Layer | Technology | Responsibility | | --- | --- | --- | | Desktop host | Rust · Tauri 2 | Native commands, transactions, progress and lifecycle | | Interface | React 19 · TypeScript · Cromma UI | Forms, previews and execution results | | Platform bridges | AppKit · Security · CoreLocation · Linux / Windows Rust | Platform permissions and system integration | | Companion browser | Fingerprint Chromium | Dedicated profile and real browser measurements | | Separate Network Skill | Python standard library · OpenSSH · Bash · Xray | AI-managed private configuration, approved remote setup and server/client verification | | Localization | YAML · Vite | Build-time English/Chinese catalogs |
Repository map ```text assets/ Compressed brand logos and pixel-art DMG background src/ Desktop UI, browser test page and localization src-tauri/src/ Rust commands and transaction boundaries src-tauri/native/ Small macOS API bridges browser-runtime/ Engine metadata, launcher, entitlements and licenses scripts/ Icons, local builds and installation helpers skills/ Installable AI Network Skill and its execution scripts packaging/arch/ Native Arch Linux PKGBUILD and desktop entry docs/ README artwork and platform development guides vendor/cromma-ui/ Vendored interface components ``` The large browser application and archive are generated/runtime inputs, excluded from Git. `CLAUDE.md` files map module boundaries; source headers describe inputs, outputs and responsibilities.
## Development ### Prerequisites On Linux, follow [Linux setup](docs/linux.md). On macOS, use an Apple Silicon Mac with Xcode Command Line Tools, stable Rust and Bun. Follow [Tauri's macOS prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/#macos) for the native toolchain. The browser engine is an external build input. `python3 scripts/fetch-browser.py` downloads the pinned macOS arm64 **Fingerprint Chromium 148.0.7778.215** engine from the [upstream project](https://github.com/adryfish/fingerprint-chromium), verifies its SHA-256 and preserves its bundle structure and notices. Browser runtime binaries are not included in the source repository. From your checkout: ```sh bun install --frozen-lockfile python3 scripts/fetch-browser.py sh scripts/make-icons.sh sh scripts/package-browser.sh bun run tauri dev ``` Local builds are for development and testing; they are not official project downloads. ### Fast local build and install (macOS) ```sh bun run dev:install ``` This builds a debug app with the embedded UI, uses local ad-hoc signatures and installs/starts both apps. It does not use Apple credentials or create an installer. It preserves profiles and settings. The development installer accepts only locally built debug apps; downloaded installers still require the normal signature and Gatekeeper checks. ### Build ```sh MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.0 \ bun run tauri build --bundles app --features custom-protocol ``` The host bundle is written to `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/CCBaga-A.app`. The companion bundle remains at `browser-runtime/Browser.app` until copied to Applications as `CCBaga-B.app`. Production builds require `custom-protocol` to load the embedded UI. Compilation without it fails explicitly, preventing an installed app from depending on the development server. ### Checks ```sh bun run build bun test MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.0 \ cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml python3 scripts/test-sign-browser.py python3 skills/ccbaga-network/scripts/test_network.py bash -n skills/ccbaga-network/scripts/setup-vps.sh ``` Pull requests run the existing frontend, native Rust, offline Skill and npm skill-installation checks on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows, plus the relevant platform regression tests. The workflow uses a read-only token, no signing secrets and no artifact uploads; it does not publish releases or download the browser engine. Complete engine and installer validation remains part of the separate delivery checks. The identity UI simulation uses 40 fictitious accounts, mocked Tauri IPC and an isolated headless context with external requests blocked. It covers card navigation, retention choices, switching, irreversible-delete alerts, failure recovery and both languages. Run `bun run test:identities` with Node.js 22.23.2 or later after preparing the pinned browser engine. The browser receives a temporary HOME/XDG configuration. Native archive tests use temporary SQLite databases and files; the macOS credential bridge is also checked against a separate disposable Keychain. Automated tests exercise disposable fixtures and local test servers. They do not deploy a real VPS, delete your Claude account data or perform administrator-authorized system changes. Real SSH connectivity, client-side TUN routing and permission-dependent operations require validation in the target environment. ## Data & permissions - **Identities are local.** Login state is archived before switching. You choose which personal data stays in the workspace and which is stored with the identity. Actual project source and cloud-side account records are outside this scope. - **Secrets stay out of UI logs.** The apps have no SSH key picker or server deployment command. After explicit confirmation, the native identity vault reads only the recognized default Claude credentials needed for restoration; credential contents never enter the GUI, command-line arguments or network. The separate Skill uses private local files and temporary private PEM copies (0600 on POSIX, verified user-only NTFS ACLs on Windows); data supplied to your coding agent is subject to that agent provider’s handling. - **Network checks make real requests.** Exit detection uses `ipwho.is` with `ipapi.co` as a fallback on the same route. IP location is a service estimate. - **Remote changes are explicit.** The separate Skill contacts only the VPS you provide after server-change approval. Required credentials remain in private local/server configuration, outside Git and public logs. - **Permissions are feature-specific.** Timezone changes require macOS administrator authorization. Keychain access follows system prompts. Location controls may require Accessibility permission or a manual action in System Settings. Custom `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` locations are not automatically included in the default identity scope. The app reports this limitation rather than silently claiming they were switched. ## Contributing Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Small, focused changes with clear behavior and relevant checks are welcome. For bug reports, include the operating system and version, app version, operation and sanitized error; never attach private keys, passwords or subscription URLs. ## License & credits CCBaga's original project code is released under the **[MIT License](LICENSE)**. Third-party code and binaries retain their own terms; see [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). Built with [Tauri](https://tauri.app/), [React](https://react.dev/) and [Fingerprint Chromium](https://github.com/adryfish/fingerprint-chromium), with a native macOS implementation of Claude maintenance workflows. Cleanup discovery was informed by the [claude-cleanup skill](https://github.com/suyuan2022/suyuan-skill/tree/main/claude-cleanup).
An independent project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or Apple.
